text: Constipation (scant, dry feces) commonly affects pregnant sows, and any high-fever disease (CSF, PRRS) reduces appetite and causes it too. Moving a sow to the maternity pen 7–10 days before delivery causes stress and temporary appetite loss — some farmers wrongly cut feed at this point thinking it will 'help' delivery, but constipation actually raises the risk of difficult delivery, E. coli contamination of milk, and MMA. Better approach: move the sow at least 10 days before farrowing (she typically eats normally again after 3–4 days) and do not reduce feed before delivery — increasing to up to 4 kg is actually better, preventing constipation and supplying extra energy for labor (fat sow body condition should be managed across the whole pregnancy instead, since cutting feed only in the last week doesn't change body condition but can reduce piglet birth weight and complicate delivery). Direct treatment: make the sow walk, offer fresh fodder, and give paraffin oil (300 ml/day). If constipation persists despite normal eating, check the feed formula's fiber content — wheat bran (especially lower-grade) is the best fiber source to add.
